name: evolve
conclusion: evolve (Act) specifies 4 of 5 categories: 10+ autonomy limits, 1 clarification rule, 5 validation rules, 2 escalation rules; none for approval gates. Strongest: autonomy limits.

autonomy_limits.conclusion: 10+ autonomy limits (10 mandatory, 0 advisory; 4 conditional), mostly list: unattended edits to critical skills; asking for confirmation, clarification or approval; asking the user during execution.

statements.quote: Critical skills listed in `docs/contracts/critical-skills.txt` reject unattended edits; use `--allow-critical` only when Bo is supervising that critical edit.
Do NOT ask the user for confirmation, clarification, or approval at any point.
| Ask the user anything during execution | Evolve is fully autonomous — questions break the loop | Make best judgment, report in teardown |
When a program contract exists, prefer work that can land wholly inside mutable scope. Do not silently widen scope around immutable files.
candidate work that clearly requires immutable-scope edits is not eligible for direct execution
if the selected item is inherently out of scope, escalate it or convert it into durable follow-up work instead of invoking `$rpi` and hoping discovery widens scope
Do not select work that is obviously outside mutable scope.
If a bead or goal would require edits under immutable scope, escalate it or convert it into durable follow-up work instead of launching `$rpi`.
Do NOT intervene, ask questions, or pause between phases.

clarification_rules.conclusion: 1 clarification rule (1 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly list: missing required execution profile fields.

statements.quote: If the repo execution profile is present but missing required fields, stop or downgrade with an explicit warning before cycle 1. Do not silently invent repo policy.

validation.conclusion: 5 validation rules (5 mandatory, 0 advisory; 3 conditional), mostly prose: project build and test bundle; declared validation_commands; program contract validation_commands.

statements.quote: After execution, run the project build+test bundle.
If the repo execution profile declared `validation_commands`, run them.
If a repo-local program contract exists, run its `validation_commands` too, de-duplicated and in declared order after the repo bootstrap checks.
Treat program `stop_conditions` as per-cycle done criteria.
Do not mark claimed work consumed, completed, or productive until both the stop conditions and the regression gate pass.

escalation.conclusion: 2 escalation rules (2 mandatory, 0 advisory; 1 conditional), mostly list: structurally invalid program file; FAIL or non-convergence.

statements.quote: If the program file exists but is structurally invalid, stop or downgrade with an explicit warning before cycle 1. Do not silently ignore a broken operator contract.
FAIL or non-convergence → write STOP citing the verdict path.
